info.name: MolochAI API
info.description:
Requests and tests for the MolochAI API: the model list, the account, chat completions (plain, streamed, tool calling, image input) and the error responses. The tests check the documented response shapes, never the wording of a reply, so the same collection runs against the real API and against the mock server from https://github.com/Moloch-AI/uncensored-ai-api.

## Setup

1. Import this collection and the two environments from the repository's `postman/` folder.
2. Real API: select the **MolochAI API** environment and put your API key in `apiKey`, a secret variable. Keys are created at https://dash.molochai.dev/account?utm_source=github&utm_medium=oss&utm_campaign=uncensored-ai-api. Chat requests use your plan's quota.
3. Mock server: start it with `node mock-server/server.mjs` in a clone of the repository (or `npx github:Moloch-AI/uncensored-ai-api`) and select the **MolochAI mock** environment. No key and no network needed. Its replies are canned text, not model output.

Keep the key in an environment, never in the collection: collections get exported and shared. Keys are not scoped (a key can read account details and create invoices) and do not expire on a timer.

## Variables

| Variable | Set in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | collection, environments | Base URL of the `/v1` requests. Default `https://api.molochai.dev/api/v1`. |
| `apiKey` | environments | Bearer token for the collection's auth. |
| `model` | collection | Model id for the chat requests. Default `glm-5.3-flash`. Pick an id with `available: true` from **List models**. |
| `accountUrl` | derived | `/api/auth/me` lives outside `/api/v1`. The collection's pre-request script derives it from `baseUrl` by replacing the trailing `/v1` with `/auth/me`. Set it yourself only if your base URL does not end in `/v1`. |
| `isMock` | mock environment | `true` lets the **Mock only** folder run. With any other environment its requests are skipped. |

## Tests

The collection's test script runs after every request. Error bodies must have the shape documented for their status (A `{"error": {...}}`, B `{"message", "errors"}`, C `{"message"}`, or not JSON for a 524). `X-RateLimit-*` and `Retry-After` must be whole numbers. Each `chat.completion` must have choices and usage. Each stream must end with `data: [DONE]`, with a usage chunk (`"choices": []`) before it unless an error event ended the stream. Each request then checks its own status and fields.

Run the whole collection with the Collection Runner or with newman. Against the real API, 11 requests run (the mock-only ones are skipped); the API allows 60 requests per minute per account.

## Limits worth knowing

- `max_tokens` is accepted (1 to 65536) but has no effect: the plan's output cap per reply is always used.
- `stop`, `n`, `seed`, `response_format`, `top_k`, `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `logprobs`, `logit_bias`, `user` and `stream_options` are dropped without an error. There is no JSON mode: ask for JSON in the prompt and validate the reply.
- Reasoning and its effort are fixed per model; no request parameter changes them.

The models have reduced refusal behavior, not none: they still sometimes decline, and they are not more accurate. The Acceptable Use Policy applies: https://molochai.dev/acceptable-use?utm_source=github&utm_medium=oss&utm_campaign=uncensored-ai-api. Documentation: https://molochai.dev/docs?utm_source=github&utm_medium=oss&utm_campaign=uncensored-ai-api

item.name: Models and account
item.description: Requests that do not run a model and cost no tokens. `GET /models` is behind the plan check (402 without a plan or credit). `GET /api/auth/me` is not behind the email or quota checks, so it still answers when the other requests fail and shows why (`plan`, `tier`, `email_verified`).

request.description:
`GET /models`: the public catalog, and for each model whether a server is serving it right now (`available`). `name` and `available` are MolochAI extensions to the OpenAI format.

Use one of these ids for the `model` variable. The catalog can change and there is no version pinning, so fetch it instead of hardcoding ids. Model details: https://molochai.dev/models?utm_source=github&utm_medium=oss&utm_campaign=uncensored-ai-api

const stringOrNull = (value) => value === null || typeof value === 'string';
pm.expect(stringOrNull(account[key]), `${key} is a string or null`).to.equal(true);
pm.test('each model has a context_limit (null when no server serves it)', () => {

request.description:
`GET /api/auth/me`: the account behind the key. `plan`, `tier` (`payg` when running on credit with no plan), `credit_usd`, `email_verified`, and for each model a `context_limit`: the smaller of the plan's limit and the serving server's limit, or null when nothing serves the model.

The path is outside `/api/v1`, so the URL is `{{accountUrl}}`. The collection's pre-request script derives it from `baseUrl` by replacing the trailing `/v1` with `/auth/me`: `https://api.molochai.dev/api/v1` becomes `https://api.molochai.dev/api/auth/me`. If your base URL does not end in `/v1`, set `accountUrl` yourself.

item.name: Chat completions
item.description:
`POST /chat/completions`. On the real API these requests run a model and count against your plan's quota.

Parameters that reach the model: `model`, `messages`, `stream`, `temperature` (0 to 2), `top_p` (0 to 1), `tools` and `tool_choice`. `max_tokens` is accepted but has no effect, and other OpenAI parameters are dropped (see **Ignored parameters**). Reasoning and its effort are fixed per model.

The gateway puts a short identity system message first. If your first message is a system message, the identity text goes above yours in the same message and yours is kept.

Prefer streaming for long replies: Cloudflare in front of the API gives up on a plain request after about 100 seconds (524).

exec: pm.test('200 with a chat.completion for the model you asked for', () => {
pm.expect(body.model, 'model is always the public id you sent').to.equal(pm.variables.get('model'));
pm.test('the answer is text, with finish_reason stop or length', () => {

request.description:
A plain request: one JSON `chat.completion` comes back when the reply is complete. Thinking models also return `message.reasoning_content`. If the serving server leaves reasoning inline, `content` starts with a `<think>...</think>` block on a plain request: the gateway strips those only while streaming.

`model` in the reply is always the id you sent. `usage.total_tokens` includes reasoning and is what counts against the quota.

exec: pm.test('no error event; the answer arrived as delta.content', () => {

request.description:
The same endpoint with `"stream": true`. The reply arrives as server-sent events (`Content-Type: text/event-stream`), in this order: a chunk with `delta.role`, `delta.reasoning_content` chunks (thinking models), `delta.content` chunks, a chunk with `finish_reason`, a usage chunk whose `choices` is empty, then `data: [DONE]`. Lines starting with `:` are comments, such as the `: ka` keep-alive or `: queued · position 2 of 3 · waiting 4s` while the request waits for a slot. Usage is always sent.

What Postman shows: the desktop app recognizes `text/event-stream` and lists the events in the response pane as they arrive, instead of one JSON body.

The tests run after the stream has ended. The collection's test script reads the raw stream with `pm.response.text()` and parses it the way a client has to: skip comment lines, stop at `[DONE]`, check each payload for an `error` key, and check for an empty `choices` before indexing it. newman and the CI of this repository run them that way.

item.name: Tool calling 1: the model calls a tool

exec: pm.test('200 and the model called a tool (finish_reason "tool_calls")', () => {
pm.expect(choice.finish_reason, 'the model answered in text instead; it decides whether to call a tool').to.equal(
pm.test('each call has an id, type "function", the declared name and JSON arguments', () => {
// arguments is a JSON string. Parse it, then validate it against the tool's schema:
// a model can produce invalid JSON or leave out a required field.
// Keep the assistant message exactly as received (tool_calls, and reasoning_content
// when present) for "Tool calling 2", which sends it back with the tool result.

request.description:
Offers one tool in the OpenAI format. When the model calls it, the reply has `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`, `content: null` and `message.tool_calls`. `function.arguments` is a JSON string: parse it, then validate it against your schema, because a model can produce invalid JSON or leave out a required field.

The model decides whether to call the tool, and `tool_choice` is passed to the serving server unchanged. If the model answers in text instead, the first test fails and says so.

In a stream, a tool call arrives whole in one chunk on this API. Other OpenAI-compatible providers send it in fragments, so join fragments by `index` anyway.

The test script keeps the assistant message for **Tool calling 2**.

item.name: Tool calling 2: send the tool result

exec: // This request sends back the assistant message from "Tool calling 1" exactly as
// received, then a role "tool" message whose tool_call_id answers the call.
// If "Tool calling 1" has not run, an example assistant message stands in for it.
pm.test('200 and a text answer (finish_reason stop or length)', () => {

request.description:
Continues the conversation with three messages: the user's question, the assistant message from **Tool calling 1** exactly as it came back, and a `role: "tool"` message whose `tool_call_id` answers the call. Sending the assistant message back unchanged includes its `reasoning_content`, so a thinking model keeps its reasoning across turns.

`{{toolTurnAssistant}}` stands in the body without quotes because it holds a whole JSON object. The tool result here is made up; in your code it is what your function returned.

If you send this request without running **Tool calling 1** first, its pre-request script uses an example assistant message instead.

A user message whose `content` is an array of parts: a text part and an `image_url` part holding a base64 data URL (a 64x64 PNG: a red square on white).

The gateway forwards image parts unchanged. They work only when the model takes images according to its model card AND the server serving it has vision enabled. Per their cards (checked on 2026-11-07), `glm-5.3-flash`, `gemma4-26b-a4b-qat` and `qwen3.8-27b-uncensored` take images; the others take text only. When either condition is missing, expect an error or a reply that did not see the image. Video input is not documented.

The mock does not look at images: it answers from the text parts.

exec: pm.test('200: the dropped parameters cause no error', () => {

request.description:
Parameters the API accepts without applying them. None of them causes an error:

- `max_tokens` is accepted (1 to 65536) but has no effect: the plan's output cap per reply is always used (https://molochai.dev/pricing?utm_source=github&utm_medium=oss&utm_campaign=uncensored-ai-api). A reply that hits the cap ends with `finish_reason: "length"` and the notice `[Response is too large for your current plan. Try a smaller request.]`.
- `n`, `stop`, `seed`, `response_format`, `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty` and `user` are dropped, as are `top_k`, `logprobs`, `logit_bias` and `stream_options`. So there is one choice, no stop sequence and no seed.
- There is no JSON mode: `response_format` does nothing. Ask for JSON in the prompt and validate what comes back.

item.name: Mock only ([mock:*] markers and special keys)
item.description:
Needs the mock server (`node mock-server/server.mjs` in a clone of https://github.com/Moloch-AI/uncensored-ai-api) and the **MolochAI mock** environment. Each request puts a `[mock:*]` marker in the last user message, or uses one of the mock's special keys, so that the mock answers the way the real API does when something goes wrong.

To the real API the markers are plain text: the request would reach a model and use your quota. So this folder's pre-request script skips every request in it unless `isMock` is `true`, which only the mock environment sets.

All markers and keys: https://github.com/Moloch-AI/uncensored-ai-api/blob/main/docs/mock-server.md
